problem: What is the value of $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{4})+2$ at its local maximum points?
worked_solution:
On a negative branch of the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x\le -1.
$$

The points where $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=-1$ are local maximums of the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$ 

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{4})\le -1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $\frac{1}{2}$ and adding $2$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{sec}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{4})\le -1 \\  & \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{4})\le -\frac{1}{2} \\  & \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{4})+2\le -\frac{1}{2}+2 \\  & f(x)\le \frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\frac{3}{2}$ at the local maximum points.
